name: Dev Dispatch — tree builder (decompose→review convergence loop)
description: When a spec card completes, route it: bugs to debugger, research to scout, ops to ops, pre-made tickets to PO parse; everything else through the architect gate (architect stamps tech stack from tech-preferences.json → setup scaffolds configs/<lang>/ → PO decompose → milestones). Replaces the old cron-based dispatch.

nodes.body_template:
## Architecture gate — triage spec before decomposition

**Spec card:** ${trigger.card_id}
**Title:** ${trigger.title}
**Spec body:**

${trigger.card_body}

You are the architect. Load your `architecture-gate` skill. Run the five-question blast-radius triage on this spec.

### What to do

1. Read the spec above (problem statement, user stories, acceptance criteria).
2. Triage with the five-question rubric. Assign a tier (T0–T3).
3. For T1+: decide the tech stack by reading `~/.hermes-teams/startup/tech-preferences.json`. Match the spec to a recipe, use its toolkits. Write an ADR if deviating from preferences.
4. Write the spec to a file at the project repo (extract the repo path from the spec body — look for `Repo:` or a filesystem path). Add `## Implementation Decisions` and `## Testing Decisions` sections with your architecture decisions. Append the stamp line.
5. If no repo path is in the spec body, write the spec to `SPEC.md` in your workspace.

### Complete with metadata

```
{verdict: "stamped", tier: "T0|T1|T2", artifacts: ["ADR-001", ...] or [], approval: "waved-through|adr-recorded", spec_file: "<path to stamped spec file>", tech_stack: "<languages and tools from tech-preferences.json>", testing_decisions: "<one-line>"}
```

Escalation: T2 — first read this project's `t2_approval` in ~/.hermes-teams/startup/active-projects.json (match by board, else repo path). `auto` → complete as done with approval: "auto-approved-config" (ceremony still mandatory, record synthesis + dissent in ADRs); `human`/absent → block the card with reason `escalated-t2:` naming what needs sign-off. T3 — always block with `T3 handback-wayfinder:` (too large to be one decision; hand back for decomposition — never auto-approved).

### Artifact classification (REQUIRED)

Classify the deliverable in `artifact_type`: webapp (UI in a browser), tui (terminal UI), cli (commands only, no interactive screens), api (no user-facing surface), library. UI-bearing types (webapp, tui) route through the design gate before any ticket may fire.

## Design gate — hold UI tickets until the design is approved

**Title:** ${trigger.title}
**Repo:** ${trigger.card_body}
**Artifact type:** ${nodes.route-architect.output.artifact_type}
**Spec file:** ${nodes.route-architect.output.spec_file}

This is a UI project. Before ANY ticket may fire, the design must be produced and adversarially reviewed. You wire that barrier now — deterministic, no improvisation.

### Step 1: Create the design gate card (holds every UI ticket)

- `title`: "[design-done] ${trigger.title} — design approved"
- `assignee`: "workflow-gate" (control-plane lane — dispatcher never spawns it; do NOT work it)
- `body`: "Design gate for this project. The design-gate workflow's design-close step completes this card ONLY after the design artifacts (ui-spec, tokens, mockups) pass adversarial review. All UI tickets wait on this card. Do NOT work this card."

Record its id: `design_gate_id`.

### Step 2: Create + complete the [design] trigger card (fires the design-gate workflow)

- `title`: "[design] ${trigger.title}"
- `assignee`: "designer"
- `body`: "Repo: <repo path>\n\nSpec: <spec file path>\n\nDESIGN GATE: <design_gate_id>\n\nTech stack: ${nodes.route-architect.output.tech_stack}\n\nProduce the four design artifacts per the design-gate workflow."

Then COMPLETE it via the CLI (it is a trigger card — nothing works it; completing fires the design-gate workflow. The CLI is the orchestrator path — the kanban_complete tool would refuse ownership):

```
hermes kanban --board ${trigger.board} complete <design-card-id> --result "design trigger — workflow takes over"
```

### Step 3: Park YOUR card until the design gate closes

```
hermes kanban --board ${trigger.board} link <design_gate_id> <this-card-id>
hermes kanban --board ${trigger.board} block <this-card-id> waiting_for_design:<design_gate_id> --kind dependency
```

You are dependency-parked: when design-close completes the gate, you auto-promote and are re-dispatched. On re-dispatch: verify the gate is done (`hermes kanban show <design_gate_id>`), then complete.

### Completion metadata

```
{design_gate: "<design_gate_id>", design_done: true, artifact_type: "${nodes.route-architect.output.artifact_type}"}
```

DO NOT design yourself. DO NOT implement.

## Project setup — scaffold tooling and hygiene files

**Repo:** ${trigger.card_body}
**Tech stack:** ${nodes.route-architect.output.tech_stack}
**Spec file:** ${nodes.route-architect.output.spec_file}

The architect has decided the tech stack. Your job is to set up the project with proper tooling BEFORE any feature tickets start.

### What to do

1. Read the tech preferences at `~/.hermes-teams/startup/tech-preferences.json` to understand the preferred tooling for the chosen stack.
2. Read the spec file at `${nodes.route-architect.output.spec_file}` to confirm the tech stack.
3. Based on the tech stack, copy the appropriate config files from `~/.hermes-teams/startup/scripts/workflow_engine/configs/` into the project repo.

### Setup by language

Detect the language from the architect's tech_stack output. Copy configs from the matching `configs/<language>/` directory:

- **Python** (`configs/python/`): pyproject.toml (replace `${PROJECT_NAME}` and `${PROJECT_DESCRIPTION}`), ruff.toml, Makefile, conftest.py, .gitignore
- **Rust** (`configs/rust/`): Cargo.toml additions, clippy.toml, rustfmt.toml, Makefile, .gitignore
- **TypeScript** (`configs/node/`): package.json, tsconfig.json, biome.json, Makefile, .gitignore
- **Go** (`configs/go/`): .golangci.yml, Makefile, .gitignore

If no configs exist for the language, create minimal ones following the same pattern (linter config, formatter config, Makefile with lint/format/test/check targets, .gitignore).

Always append global patterns from `configs/_shared/.gitignore.global` to `.gitignore`.

### Verify

After copying, run the linter and formatter for the detected language:
- Python: `ruff check . || true` and `ruff format --check . || true`
- Rust: `cargo clippy -- -D warnings || true` and `cargo fmt --check || true`
- TypeScript: `npx biome check . || true`
- Go: `golangci-lint run || true`

If the repo already has config files, MERGE your sections into the existing file rather than overwriting. Do not destroy existing config.

### Completion metadata

```
{setup_done: true, files_created: ["list"], files_merged: ["list"], language: "detected", linter: "detected", formatter: "detected", test_runner: "detected", has_gitignore: true}
```

## Decompose spec into tickets — loop_engine converge loop

**Title:** ${trigger.title}
**Architect spec file:** ${nodes.route-architect.output.spec_file}
**Tech stack:** ${nodes.route-architect.output.tech_stack}
**Testing decisions:** ${nodes.route-architect.output.testing_decisions}

You are the product-owner. DO NOT implement.

The architect has already reviewed the spec and stamped architecture decisions into the spec file above. Read that file — it contains Implementation Decisions (tech stack, data model, storage, CLI surface) and Testing Decisions that each ticket MUST inherit.

### Call loop_engine — it handles the ENTIRE loop

Call `loop_engine` with:

- `goal`: "Decompose spec into complete, atomic ticket plan: ${trigger.title}"
- `runner`: "product-owner"
- `max_iterations`: 3

- `execution`: {
    title: "[plan-exec] Decompose spec into ticket plan",
    body: "Read the stamped spec file at ${nodes.route-architect.output.spec_file}. This file has Implementation Decisions (tech stack, data model, storage, CLI surface) and Testing Decisions stamped by the architect. Each ticket MUST inherit these decisions. Load your to-tickets skill. Produce a TICKET PLAN: a numbered list of tickets. For each ticket include: title, what-to-build (acceptance criteria with specific tech from the architect decisions), and blocked-by (dependency numbers). Output the complete ticket plan.",
    assignee: "product-owner",
    skill: "to-tickets"
  }

- `verifier`: {
    title: "[plan-review] Review ticket plan for completeness and atomicity",
    body: "You are reviewing a ticket plan against the stamped spec file at ${nodes.route-architect.output.spec_file}. The architect stamped Implementation Decisions and Testing Decisions — every ticket must be consistent with them. Check THREE dimensions:

1. MISSING FEATURES: Does every spec requirement have a corresponding ticket?
2. SCOPE CREEP: Does every ticket trace to a spec requirement?
3. NEED BREAKDOWN: Is every ticket atomic (junior-dev-in-one-sitting, testable ACs, single concern)?
4. ARCHITECTURE CONSISTENCY: Does each ticket inherit the architect's tech stack and data model decisions?

Complete with metadata dod_verdict as a SIMPLE dict: {dod_met: true|false, recommendation: \"advance\"|\"replan\", gaps: [\"specific gap 1\", ...]}. Do NOT include behaviors, defect_traces, evidence, or any other arrays. Keep it minimal.",
    assignee: "verifier",
    metric_type: "ground_truth"
  }

### What happens on each promotion

EVERY time you auto-promote (loop_engine dependency-park ends and you are re-dispatched):

1. Call `loop_engine` AGAIN with the SAME parameters above (same goal, same execution, same verifier). Do NOT change the arguments.
2. loop_engine reads the previous verdict and decides:
   - DoD MET (PASS): it tells you to advance. Then you read the final plan and create ticket cards (below).
   - DoD NOT MET (FAIL): it creates a fresh exec + verify pair (replan). You are dependency-parked again. Do nothing — just wait for the next promotion.
   - HARD CAP: it escalates. Complete your card with what you have.

DO NOT read verdicts yourself. DO NOT fix the plan yourself. DO NOT skip calling loop_engine on any promotion. CALL IT EVERY TIME. loop_engine is the loop — you are just its driver.

### Create ticket cards — ONLY after loop_engine says advance

When loop_engine returns decision=advance (DoD met):

Read the final ticket plan from the last execution card. Create cards in
dependency order (Layer 0 first). EACH ticket gets TWO cards:

1. GATE card first — tracks REAL completion (the tech-lead-execute close step
   completes it only after the ticket branch is merged and all tests pass):
   - `title`: "[done-NN] <ticket title>"
   - `assignee`: "workflow-gate"
     (control-plane lane, NOT a profile — the dispatcher never spawns a worker
     on it; humans and agents must NOT work it)
   - `body`: "Completion gate for [ticket-NN] <title>. The tech-lead-execute
     close step completes this card after the ticket is merged and all tests
     pass. Do NOT work this card."

2. TRIGGER card — fires the implementation workflow:
   - `title`: "[ticket-NN] <ticket title>"
   - `assignee`: "tech-lead"
   - `body`: "This is a trigger card. Complete this card IMMEDIATELY. Do NOT
     implement. Do NOT delegate. Do NOT call kanban_chains or loop_engine. The
     next workflow (tech-lead-execute) handles all execution.\n\nGATE:
     <the [done-NN] card id from step 1>\n\n---\n\n" + the ticket's
     what-to-build (acceptance criteria)
   - `parents`: the GATE card ids of each blocked-by ticket — NEVER the
     [ticket-NN] cards. Gate cards track real completion, so a ticket that
     depends on another cannot even TRIGGER until the blocker's implementation
     workflow has fully closed (merged + tests green). Layer-0 tickets: no
     parents.

Record both ids: ticket_ids = trigger ids, gate_ids = gate ids (needed by the
milestone step).

### Completion metadata

```
{decomposed: true, ticket_count: N, ticket_ids: ["<id1>", ...], gate_ids: ["<gid1>", ...], converged: true, iterations: N}
```


### UI projects: parent triggers on the design gate

If this project went through the design gate (design gate id available as ${nodes.route-design.output.design_gate}), EVERY ticket trigger card gets the design gate id as an ADDITIONAL parent (alongside its dependency gates): a ticket cannot even TRIGGER until the design is approved. Use the exact id — do not paraphrase.

## Plan milestones from ticket dependency graph

**Title:** ${trigger.title}
**Ticket count:** ${nodes.route-decompose.output.ticket_count}
**Ticket IDs:** ${nodes.route-decompose.output.ticket_ids}
**Repo:** ${trigger.card_body}

You are the product-owner. Your job is to group the decomposed tickets into milestones. When a milestone completes, it triggers a QA + refactor pass via the milestone-gate workflow — and the NEXT milestone's entry tickets stay HELD until that QA gate passes.

### Rules for grouping

1. Read the ticket plan. Each ticket has dependencies (blocked-by).
2. Group tickets into milestones using these principles:
   - Tickets with NO dependencies between them can share a milestone (they're parallel work)
   - A ticket that depends on another should be in the SAME milestone as its dependency IF they're small, or in a LATER milestone if the dependency is foundational
   - Aim for 2-5 tickets per milestone
   - The LAST milestone should contain the final integration tickets
3. If there are only 1-3 tickets total, create a single milestone containing all of them.
4. Do NOT create more than 5 milestones.

### Create milestone cards

For EACH milestone NN (in order), create the QA gate card FIRST, then the
milestone card:

1. QA GATE card — this milestone's pass marker. It holds back the next
   milestone until QA + refactor complete:
   - `title`: "[qa-done-NN] <short description>: QA gate"
   - `assignee`: "workflow-gate" (control-plane lane — the dispatcher never
     spawns a worker on it; humans and agents must NOT work it)
   - `body`: "Milestone NN QA gate. The milestone-gate workflow's gate-close
     step completes this card ONLY after this milestone's QA passes and its
     refactor cycle completes. Milestone NN+1 entry tickets wait on this
     card. Do NOT work this card."

2. MILESTONE card — call `kanban_create`:
   - `title`: "[milestone-NN] <short description>: ${trigger.title}"
   - `assignee`: "product-owner"
   - `body`: "**Repo:** ${trigger.card_body}\n\nQA gate: <the [qa-done-NN] card id from step 1>\n\nMilestone NN scope (what THIS milestone delivers): <list ONLY the user stories / features this milestone ships — derived from its tickets, NOT the full project spec>.\n\nDeferred to later milestones: <list user stories NOT in this milestone, or write \"none\" if this is the final milestone>.\n\nContains tickets: <list ticket numbers and titles>. This card auto-completes when all its parent GATES are done (i.e. every ticket truly merged). Completing this card triggers the milestone-gate workflow (QA + refactor)."
   - `parents`: list of GATE card IDs ([done-NN]) in this milestone — NOT the [ticket-NN] trigger cards. Gates are completed by each ticket's tech-lead-execute close step (merge + tests green), so this milestone auto-promotes only after every ticket's implementation workflow has FULLY closed — never while verification/fixes are still in flight.

The milestone card stays in `todo` until all parent tickets complete, then auto-promotes.

### Wire the milestone barrier (milestone 2 and later)

For EACH milestone NN >= 2, call the `group_cards` tool (kanban_group plugin)
EXACTLY with this shape — deterministic wiring, do NOT improvise links by
hand:

```
group_cards({
  key: "m<NN>",
  members: [{card: "<ENTRY ticket trigger id>", done: "<that ticket's [done-NN] gate id>"}, ...one per entry ticket...],
  pre: [{gate: "<the [qa-done-(NN-1)] card id of milestone NN-1>"}]
})
```

- ENTRY ticket of milestone NN = a ticket whose blocked-by gates are ALL from
  earlier milestones (or it has no blocked-by). A ticket blocked by a
  SAME-milestone ticket is NOT an entry — its blocker's gate already holds it.
- Take trigger ids and gate ids from the decompose card's recorded
  ticket_ids / gate_ids (same source as the milestone parents).
- Milestone 1 gets NO group_cards call (nothing to wait on).
- The result must have status "wired" (or "recovered" on a retry). On an
  error, follow the result's error.repair instruction EXACTLY — re-calling
  group_cards with the same arguments is always safe (idempotent).

### Completion metadata

```
{milestone_count: N, milestone_ids: ["<id1>", ...], qa_gate_ids: ["<qg1>", ...], milestones: [{number: 1, tickets: ["t_xxx", ...], entry_tickets: ["t_yyy", ...], qa_gate: "<id>", description: "<short>"}]}
```

DO NOT call kanban_chains. DO NOT implement.

## Parse pre-made tickets — create cards with dependencies

**Source card:** ${trigger.card_id}
**Title:** ${trigger.title}

You are the product-owner. DO NOT decompose. DO NOT plan. DO NOT implement. Your ONLY job is to parse the ticket definitions from the source card body and create one kanban card per ticket with correct dependencies.

### Phase 1: Parse

Read the source card body. It contains pre-made ticket definitions in this format:

```
## Ticket NN — <title>
**Blocked by:** NN, NN (or "none")
**Body:** <what to build>
```

Parse each ticket block. Extract: number, title, blocked-by list, body text.

### Phase 2: Create cards (CRITICAL)

CREATE IN DEPENDENCY ORDER: Layer 0 (no blockers) first, then Layer 1, etc.
EACH ticket gets TWO cards:

1. GATE card first — tracks REAL completion:
   - `title`: "[done-NN] <ticket title>"
   - `assignee`: "workflow-gate" (control-plane lane — dispatcher never spawns it; do NOT work it)
   - `body`: "Completion gate for [ticket-NN]. The tech-lead-execute close step completes this card after the ticket is merged and all tests pass."

2. TRIGGER card — fires the implementation workflow:
   - `title`: "[ticket-NN] <ticket title>"
   - `assignee`: "tech-lead"
   - `body`: the ticket's body text (what to build), PREFIXED with:
     "This is a trigger card. Complete this card IMMEDIATELY. Do NOT implement. The next workflow (tech-lead-execute) handles all execution.\n\nGATE: <the [done-NN] card id>\n\n---\n\n"
   - `parents`: the GATE card ids for each "Blocked by" entry — NEVER the [ticket-NN] cards.

Each ticket fires tech-lead-execute when its trigger card completes; dependent
tickets cannot fire until their blockers' gates close (merge + tests green).

DO NOT call kanban_chains. DO NOT call loop_engine. DO NOT decompose. DO NOT implement.

### Completion metadata

After creating ALL ticket cards, complete this card with:
```
{decomposed: true, ticket_count: N, ticket_ids: ["<id1>", "<id2>", ...]}
```
